headline: Google Ads for solar installers in Delhi NCR: a city-by-city setup
card_title: Google Ads for solar installers in Delhi NCR
card_text: How to structure Google Ads across Delhi, Gurugram, Noida, Ghaziabad and Faridabad: campaigns by state and DISCOM, NCR keywords, location targeting and negatives.
crumb: Google Ads for solar in NCR
intro:
Google Ads for solar installers in Delhi NCR goes wrong in a predictable way: one campaign, one big radius, one landing page, and a search terms report full of job seekers, portal logins and clicks from cities the survey team never visits. The fix isn't a bigger budget. It's a structure that matches how NCR actually works, with three states, several DISCOMs and buyers who search by locality.

This guide gives you that structure: how to split campaigns by state and DISCOM, a keyword list for Delhi, Gurugram, Noida, Greater Noida, Ghaziabad and Faridabad, location settings that stop border spill, the NCR-specific negatives, and how to compare cities on cost per site visit.

sections.h2: Why Google Ads for solar installers in Delhi NCR needs its own structure
sections.html:
Delhi NCR looks like one market on a map, but for a rooftop solar buyer it is three states with different subsidy rules and several different electricity companies. A homeowner in Janakpuri, one in DLF Phase 2 and one in Indirapuram may type almost the same search, yet they need different answers about who approves the net meter, what state support exists and how long the process takes.

If one campaign targets the whole of NCR with one set of ads and one landing page, the ad has to stay vague, the page can't answer the DISCOM question, and you can't see which city actually brings site visits. A structure built around NCR's real boundaries fixes all three. It also makes the budget easier to control, because you can push spend toward the cities where your survey team is strongest.

sections.h2: Split campaigns by state and DISCOM first, city second
sections.html:
Build one campaign per state, then one ad group per city or cluster of localities inside it. That way every ad and landing page can name the right electricity company and the right subsidy story. A starting map:

CampaignCities and areasDISCOM to nameWhat the landing page must answer
DelhiSouth and West Delhi, East and Central Delhi, North and North-West DelhiBSES Rajdhani, BSES Yamuna or Tata Power-DDL (NDMC for the central zone)Central PM Surya Ghar subsidy plus Delhi's own state support; DISCOM net-metering steps
Haryana NCRGurugram, FaridabadDakshin Haryana Bijli Vitran Nigam (DHBVN)Central subsidy, DHBVN net-metering process, society and builder-floor rules
UP NCRNoida, Greater Noida, GhaziabadPVVNL for most of Noida and Ghaziabad, NPCL for most of Greater NoidaCentral subsidy plus any current UP state support; PVVNL or NPCL process

Inside Delhi, split ad groups by DISCOM zone rather than by every colony. South and West Delhi fall mainly under BSES Rajdhani, East and Central Delhi under BSES Yamuna, and North and North-West Delhi under Tata Power-DDL. Confirm the DISCOM for each locality you target, because boundaries don't always follow district names.

Keep a separate brand campaign for your company name and a separate commercial campaign for factories and warehouses in places like Okhla, Udyog Vihar, Noida Phase 2 and Faridabad's industrial sectors. Commercial searches behave differently and shouldn't share a budget with homeowners.

sections.h2: A Delhi NCR keyword list built from how people actually search
sections.html:
Start each city ad group with phrase and exact match versions of a few patterns, then let the search terms report tell you what to add. Useful patterns for NCR:

  • Service + city: "rooftop solar installation gurgaon", "solar panel for home noida", "solar company in faridabad"
  • Service + locality: "solar installer dwarka", "rooftop solar indirapuram", "solar panel greater noida west", "solar company sohna road"
  • System size + city: "3 kw solar system price delhi", "5 kw on grid solar gurgaon"
  • Subsidy + city: "solar subsidy delhi", "pm surya ghar vendor noida", "rooftop solar subsidy haryana"
  • DISCOM + net metering: "bses net metering solar", "dhbvn solar net metering", "npcl rooftop solar"
  • Hindi and Hinglish: "ghar par solar lagwana delhi", "solar panel lagwane ka kharcha"
  • Near me: "solar installer near me", which only works if location targeting is tight

DISCOM and subsidy searches are mixed intent. Some come from buyers, many come from people checking an application or looking for a helpline. Give them their own ad group with a lower bid and a landing page that explains the process, so you can watch their cost per site visit separately.

Check volumes and suggested bids in Keyword Planner city by city. Gurugram and South Delhi often show different competition from Ghaziabad or Faridabad, and these numbers change through the year, especially before summer.

sections.h2: Location targeting across NCR's city borders
sections.html:
NCR cities sit right next to each other, so a loose setting can send a Faridabad installer clicks from South Delhi, or a Noida installer clicks from East Delhi across the Yamuna. Tighten it in four steps:

  1. Target named cities, districts or pincodes instead of one big radius around your office. A 25 km radius from central Delhi covers parts of four or five cities.
  2. Set the location option to Presence: "people in or regularly in your included locations". The broader default also includes people who show interest in a place without being there.
  3. Exclude areas you can't survey within a day, such as far parts of Sonipat, Rohtak or Bulandshahr if you don't work there.
  4. Review the location report every month and move budget toward the cities and pincodes that bring booked surveys, not just clicks.

If your team covers only part of a city, for example Gurugram's new sectors but not old Gurugram, say so in the ad. A clear "Serving Sectors 56–115" line costs nothing and stops wasted clicks.

sections.h2: Negative keywords that matter in Delhi NCR
sections.html:
Gurugram, Noida and Faridabad are large job markets with many solar companies, so job searches are a bigger leak here than in most cities. Add these negatives from day one:

  • Jobs: job, jobs, vacancy, hiring, salary, fresher, walk in, internship, naukri
  • Portals and helplines: login, status, track application, helpline, customer care, complaint, portal
  • Policy and paperwork: pdf, notification, policy document, tender, eligibility list
  • Products you don't sell: solar water heater, solar street light, solar pump, solar inverter only, solar fan
  • Trade and second hand: dealership, franchise, distributor, wholesale, used, second hand, olx
  • Utility-scale and learning: solar park, solar plant project report, course, training

Don't add "subsidy" or "net metering" as negatives. Plenty of real buyers search them; they just need their own ad group and page, as above. Review the search terms report twice a week for the first month and keep adding.

sections.h2: Ad copy for each NCR city that stays accurate
sections.html:
Because each campaign covers one state, the ads can be specific without being risky:

  • Delhi: "Rooftop Solar in South Delhi", "BSES Net Meter Paperwork Handled", "Central + Delhi Subsidy Explained"
  • Gurugram and Faridabad: "Solar for Gurugram Homes", "DHBVN Net Metering Support", "Builder Floor Solar Options"
  • Noida, Greater Noida, Ghaziabad: "Rooftop Solar in Noida", "PVVNL and NPCL Paperwork Handled", "Free Site Survey in Ghaziabad"

Use real numbers only: your actual installation count, your actual price before subsidy. PM Surya Ghar currently gives homes central assistance of up to ₹78,000, and Delhi and Uttar Pradesh have announced their own state support. Figures and conditions change, so confirm them on the official portals before they go into a headline, and keep the exact amounts on the landing page where you can update them.

Never present yourself as the government or a scheme office. Google tightened its Government documents and services policy in October 2026, and its misleading representation rules apply to every ad. Phrases such as "free solar" or "zero bill guaranteed" risk disapproval and mislead buyers. Our guide to Google Ads for solar companies covers ad assets, call tracking and bidding in more detail.

sections.h2: Budget split and ad schedule across NCR cities
sections.html:
Don't spread a small budget across all of NCR on day one. Start with the two or three cities your team serves best, give each core ad group enough budget for ten to fifteen clicks a day at its local cost per click, and add cities once those are running well.

Schedule ads for hours when someone can answer the phone. NCR homeowners often search in the evening and on Sundays, so if your team doesn't work then, switch off call assets in those hours and let the form and WhatsApp collect enquiries for a morning callback. Our solar lead generation guide for Delhi covers fast follow-up and DISCOM-based lead filters.

sections.h2: Measure cost per site visit by city
sections.html:
Cost per click and cost per lead vary by city, but what matters is cost per booked survey. Import qualified leads and site visits from your CRM or sheet as offline conversions, then compare cities each month:

Check monthlyWhat it tells you
Leads by city and ad groupWhere demand is coming from
Share of leads who own the roofWhether targeting and copy are filtering well
Site visits per cityWhere to move budget
Installations per cityWhich cities actually pay back

This is how we run solar search accounts for the 30+ solar EPCs and manufacturers we work with. Well-run rooftop campaigns bring qualified enquiries at ₹60–80 each, and solar clients at scale typically see 20–30 leads a day and 5–10 site visits a week; your numbers depend on city, offer and follow-up speed. faqs: Should a Delhi NCR solar installer run one Google Ads campaign or several?

Several. One campaign per state (Delhi, Haryana NCR, UP NCR) lets each ad and landing page name the right DISCOM and subsidy rules, and shows you which city brings site visits. Add a brand campaign and, if you sell to businesses, a separate commercial campaign.
Which electricity company should my solar ads mention in each NCR city?

In Delhi it is BSES Rajdhani, BSES Yamuna or Tata Power-DDL depending on the area, with NDMC in the central zone. Gurugram and Faridabad are served by DHBVN. Most of Noida and Ghaziabad is PVVNL, and most of Greater Noida is NPCL. Confirm the DISCOM for each locality before you name it.
How much should I spend on Google Ads for solar in Delhi NCR?

Start with two or three cities and enough daily budget for ten to fifteen clicks per core ad group at your local cost per click, which you can check in Keyword Planner. Judge results on cost per site visit after 60 to 90 days rather than on cost per click.
Can I mention the PM Surya Ghar subsidy in Google Ads?

Yes, as long as you present yourself as a private installer and use current official figures. Avoid anything that suggests you are the government, and avoid claims like free solar or a guaranteed zero bill.
Why am I getting Google Ads clicks from outside my service area?

Usually because the location option includes people interested in your area, or the radius is too wide for NCR. Switch to presence targeting, target named cities or pincodes, and exclude areas you don't serve.
